meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-13 14:00 UTC; Duration: 45 minutes; Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE); Daniel Park (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (Brightline - ML Eng); Mark Reynolds (Brightline - Platform Eng); Priya Shah (Brightline - CTO); Recording: yes; Location: Zoom
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput test results on the Brightline pilot. Discussed continuous batching behavior, observed throughput and latency tradeoffs, concurrency targets, and queueing/backpressure. Planned a longer E2E run on a dedicated pool with updated batching window and concurrency caps. Assigned action items and agreed on next check-in after the extended run.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. happy friday. quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha (Brightline - ML Eng): hey, Aisha here. Mark is on as well.
[00:12] Mark (Brightline - Platform Eng): yep Mark here.
[00:15] Priya (CTO): Priya dialed in.
[00:18] Daniel (Redwood SE): Daniel here, i'll share screen in a sec with the perf sheet.
[00:24] Sofia: cool, the goal today is to walk the latest throughput runs you did yesterday, talk config changes for continuous batching and set the target concurrency for the dedicated pool.
[00:32] Aisha: sounds good. quick note - the short run yesterday had weird p99 spikes around 800 to 1k tokens, so we're a bit nervous about tail latency for the user flows.
[00:40] Daniel: yeah we saw that too; i pulled the logs, looks like the batching window was at 20ms and we had bursty arrivals that caused some queuing, the runtime bumped concurrency to make up for it and you hit the q depth limit which pushed some requests to fall back to the hosted variant - that caused a mixing effect in latency numbers.
[01:05] Mark: when you say q depth limit, do you mean your per-worker request queue? our infra team also saw retries from the client side.
[01:12] Daniel: correct, per-worker queue. we cap the in-flight per-worker at 16 requests in this config, and the runtime also does a background continuous batcher that accumulates for up to 40ms before dispatching if traffic's low.
[01:28] Aisha: we configured client retries to exponential backoff after 200ms, maybe too aggressive for this pattern.
[01:33] Priya: important for us is steady p50 under 120ms and p95 under 400ms; if bursts push p99 to 1s it's problematic.
[01:42] Sofia: ok noted. Daniel, can you walk through the perf sheet numbers?
[01:45] Daniel: sure, sharing screen (screen share noise) - so run ID 2026-05-12-17 had sustained throughput of ~2.2k reqs/min at concurrency 32 with avg token latency 85ms, p95 370ms, p99 980ms. The longer run we did with batching window increased to 40ms got better steady throughput to ~2.6k reqs/min but slightly worse p99 in a couple windows.
[02:18] Aisha: is that because batching window increased? I'd have expected bigger window to smooth p99.
[02:23] Daniel: it's a mix - larger window aggregates more requests so GPU utilization goes up, but when traffic is bursty and queue saturation happens you see tail effects from scheduling bumps. Also KV cache warmup/evictions showed up on some sequences - the transcriber sometimes reads K V cash instead of KV cache btw - lol.
[02:46] Mark: related to capacity, how many workers were in the dedicated pool for that run?
[02:50] Daniel: we had 6 workers (N=6) in the dedicated pool, each with 16 in-flight cap. So theoretical max concurrency was 96 but effective concurrency lower due to batching windows and serialization.
[03:05] Aisha: can we try lowering per-worker in-flight to 12 and increase workers to 8? that may reduce per-worker queuing and help tail.
[03:13] Daniel: yes that tradeoff usually helps; total concurrency similar but queue depth per worker reduced. downside is more context switches but for your workload it may reduce p99.
[03:25] Priya: what's the impact on cost? more workers = more reserved GPUs right? we are watching the budget.
[03:31] Sofia: correct, increasing workers to 8 on Dedicated will increase reserved capacity cost for the slot hours, but because utilization is higher with better batching you might offset some cost per token. we'll model it in the perf sheet.
[03:45] Daniel: two knobs to test in the next run: (1) per-worker cap 12 + pool size 8; (2) batching window 30ms with stride tuning; also try enabling prefix KV sticky caching to reduce hot-key evictions.
[03:59] Aisha: sticky caching might help with the conversational flows where same user keeps context. do you have an easy toggle?
[04:05] Daniel: yes it's a runtime flag for KV placement; on private/dedicated we can enable it per-deployment but there is a warmup period.
[04:16] Mark: you also mentioned queueing/backpressure earlier - what does the client see during saturation? do we get 429s or delayed responses?
[04:23] Daniel: we push back via 429 when request queue exceeds a soft threshold; we also can configure client-side prioritized queues. In your test we saw a few 429s because your client retried aggressively which amplified bursts.
[04:38] Aisha: ok we'll relax the client retry to a 500ms base and cap at 3 retries for the next run.
[04:45] Priya: can we run a longer smoke for 2 hours during off-peak so you can capture sustained patterns?
[04:51] Daniel: yes we proposed a 2-hour E2E throughput job on staging dedicated pool, with the new knobs. we'll collect GPU metrics, queue depths, and request traces.
[05:02] Sofia: we'll also add a synthetic spike test at 10x baseline for 5 minutes to see fallback behavior.
[05:09] Aisha: good idea. also we'll share a sample of production traces (anonymized) so the traffic shape matches reality.
[05:16] Daniel: perfect. regarding concurrency targets, another option is to set route-level concurrency caps so critical routes don't starve; we can reserve some headroom.
[05:27] Mark: that might be useful - for billing endpoints we want deterministic p95 under 250ms.
[05:33] Daniel: ok we'll define two routes: 'billing' with concurrency cap 24 and 'chat' flexible. we'll include in the config diff.
[05:41] Sofia: any security or infra blockers for a 2-hour run? Mark?
[05:44] Mark: i need to double-check VPC egress quotas and our firewall for the staging pool; i'll confirm by Monday.
[05:51] Priya: also want to make sure audit logs are retained for the test since we'll need them for compliance review.
[05:56] Sofia: we can enable extended logs for the run, but will note increased storage.
[06:01] Daniel: quick question - you mentioned p99 spikes around 1s, are those correlated to specific model variants? we saw more spikes when fallback to a hosted variant happened due to capacity mismatch.
[06:12] Aisha: i think so, yes - some requests were routed to a smaller model as fallback. we should avoid fallback for critical routes.
[06:19] Daniel: we'll pin the billing route to a deterministic model and set fallback off for it.
[06:24] Sofia: okay summary: run a 2-hour E2E with per-worker 12, pool size 8, batching window 30ms, sticky KV enabled, client retry relaxed, two-route caps, and a 5-minute synthetic spike. Daniel runs and shares logs; Sofia shares config diff. Mark confirms infra. Aisha provides traces.
[06:43] Priya: timeline okay. when is the next sync?
[06:45] Sofia: we propose one week after the run - so next Friday May 22 same time?
[06:51] Aisha: works for me.
[06:53] Mark: Works.
[06:54] Daniel: noted. i'll start the job and post the run id in the shared perf sheet slack channel.
[07:00] Sofia: perfect. any final questions?
[07:03] Aisha: one last thing - can you include per-token cost estimate for the dedicated config vs hosted fallback in the perf sheet? we need that for the business case.
[07:12] Sofia: yes we'll add cost-per-token and estimated monthly cost based on projected throughput.
[07:17] Priya: thanks everyone.
[07:19] Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing. meeting adjourned.
